people.paul.role: Prisoner of Christ Jesus who writes to the saints
people.paul.relations: He sends Tychicus to tell the readers his news and to comfort them.
people.paul.meaning: Paul writes to the saints at Ephesus and prays for them. He says he is a prisoner for the Gentiles. He asks them not to lose heart over his troubles. He asks them to pray that he speaks boldly in chains. He sends Tychicus with news.
people.jesus.role: Lord who makes Jews and Gentiles one body
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him the head of the assembly. He tells husbands to love as Christ loved the assembly.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says Christ broke down the wall between Jews and Gentiles. He made both one body through the cross. Paul calls him the head of the assembly. Paul tells readers to forgive as God forgave them in Christ.
people.tychicus.role: Messenger Paul sends to tell his news
people.tychicus.relations: Paul calls him the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord.
people.tychicus.meaning: Paul sends Tychicus so the readers will know how he is doing. Tychicus will make known all things about Paul. He is also to comfort their hearts.
places.ephesus.summary: Paul writes in chapter 1 to the saints who are at Ephesus. The letter names no other place for the readers.
places.ephesus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: All six chapters are the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: The letter names Paul as its writer. The guide did not check authorship, date, manuscripts, or Greek forms. It did not check the prison setting or the full group of readers. The household commands are read inside the letter. They do not show that unequal power ended.
sources.carlson-ephesians.summary: Carlson reads the armor as resistance helped by gifts from God.
sources.carlson-ephesians.limits: This is Carlson’s own reading. The guide did not check his Greek analysis or his ancient speech comparisons. It did not check his links with Isaiah. It did not review the linked commentaries and podcasts.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-41.summary: The lesson studies shared Church work, family care, and protection from evil.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-41.limits: Coverage follows the chapters the lesson discusses. The lesson does not study chapters one and three on their own. Its use for present Church leaders is Church teaching. It is not independent historical evidence.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This Church-published atlas names towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: It supplies only the chosen reference coordinates. The earlier review record is unchanged. This source does not confirm Gospel events or exact routes.
sources.net-acts-map.summary: Opening descriptions and coordinates mark the cities named in Acts.
sources.net-acts-map.limits: These broad points do not confirm ancient events, travel paths, buildings, or coastlines. The guide did not adopt older encyclopedia claims about authorship, law, population, or exact dates.
chapters.*.mapNote: The map marks Ephesus as one city point. It shows no prison or house.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The letter gives no delivery route and does not name the prison.
